0.0.n: Names the year being discussed and connects to 年始 through の.

0.1.n: Links 今年 to 年始, specifying which year's beginning.

0.2.n: Refers to the New Year period, not necessarily New Year's Day.

0.3.n: Links 年始 to ご挨拶, identifying the occasion for the greeting.

0.4.n: The prefix ご adds respect or politeness to 挨拶.

0.5.n: Connects ご挨拶 to とき to mean the time of the greeting.

0.6.n: Combines with the preceding phrase to identify when something happened.

0.7.n: Marks the time when the event occurred.

0.8.n: Part of ですね, a polite conversational filler here rather than a separate statement.

0.9.n: Softens the pause and keeps the listener involved.

1.0.n: Points to the item the speaker is discussing.

1.1.n: Adds this item to other things that appeared or came up.

1.2.n: Past form of 出てくる, describing something appearing or entering the conversation.

1.3.n: Short for の, adding an explanatory tone before です.

1.4.n: Makes the explanation polite without changing the past tense expressed by 出てきた.

1.5.n: Highlights the information for the listener; ね then softens it.

1.6.n: Invites the listener to share the speaker's recollection.

2.1.n: With a negative expression, indicates that the action has not happened up to now.

2.2.n: Literally a bag; here it refers to the game's outer packaging.

2.3.n: Emphasizes that not even the basic step of opening the packaging has happened.

2.4.n: The て-form of 開ける connects to ねえ to describe an action not yet done.

2.5.n: Rough, casual pronunciation of ない; 開けてねえ is shortened from 開けていない.

2.7.n: Introduces the preceding quoted observation as the content of こと.

2.8.n: Packages the preceding statement as a situation the speaker can refer to.

2.9.n: Completes ということで, using that situation as the basis for what follows.

3.0.n: A conversational filler that eases into the speaker's reasoning.

3.2.n: A noun for opening sealed packaging; used with をする to express the action.

3.3.n: Marks 開封 as the action performed with する.

3.4.n: The conditional form of する; 開封をすれば sets up unboxing as a condition.

3.5.n: Adds a friendly pause after the condition.

4.0.n: Refers to the time after opening the game.

4.2.n: Refers to the board game being unboxed.

4.3.n: Marks ゲーム as what the speaker expects to play.

4.4.n: A borrowed noun that combines with する to make a verb.

4.5.n: する plus だろう expresses a prediction rather than a firm promise.

4.6.n: Frames the preceding prediction as an idea connected to the self-admonition that follows.

5.0.n: Refers back to the speaker, not to another person.

5.1.n: Links 自分 to 戒め, understood here as an admonition directed at oneself.

5.2.n: Softens 戒め so the speaker's self-admonition sounds less severe.

5.3.n: Suggests a reminder to discipline oneself and actually play the game.

5.4.n: Adds self-admonition as another purpose of making the video.

5.5.n: The て-form of 含める links this additional purpose to the main statement that follows.

6.0.n: Sets the time for the unboxing review.

6.1.n: Makes 今日 the topic, establishing what the speaker will do today.

6.3.n: A polite way to indicate the item being shown.

6.4.n: Links こちら to the following title, identifying the item being indicated.

6.6.n: Part of the game's Japanese title, modifying 電力会社.

6.8.n: Part of the game's name; combines with 会社 to mean an electricity company.

6.9.n: Part of the game's name, completing 電力会社, the Japanese title corresponding to Power Grid.

6.11.n: Part of the game edition's name, borrowed from English.

6.13.n: Part of the edition's name, emphasizing that the Japanese-language version is complete.

6.14.n: Part of the edition's name; 版 means a version or edition.

6.16.n: With ね, politely identifies the displayed game before the speaker continues.

6.17.n: Softens the identification and maintains contact with the listener.

7.0.n: Modifies レビュー directly to specify the kind of review.

7.1.n: An English borrowing used as a noun.

7.2.n: Connects 開封レビュー to ほう in a conversational softening expression.

7.3.n: In のほう, adds indirectness; it does not indicate a literal direction or comparison here.

7.4.n: Marks the unboxing review as what the speaker will present.

7.5.n: The polite お-prefixed form of 届ける combines with する to humbly describe presenting something to viewers.

7.6.n: する becomes したい to express desire; here it completes お届けしたい.

7.7.n: Marks お届けしたい as the thought expressed by 思います.

7.8.n: Polite form of 思う; with たいと, it expresses an intention gently.

0.lit: At the time of this year's New Year greeting, you know,
0.tip: Repeated の links nouns together, while ときに marks when something happened.

1.lit: This also came up, you know.
1.tip: んですよね presents an explanation while inviting the listener to share the recollection.

2.lit: Given that I haven't even opened the wrapping yet,
2.tip: 開けてねえ is rough casual speech for 開けていない, meaning the opening has not happened.

3.lit: Well, if I do the unboxing, you know,
3.tip: すれば is the if-form of する, setting up a condition for what follows.

4.lit: The idea that after that, I will probably play the game,
4.tip: だろう expresses the speaker's prediction, not a definite commitment.

5.lit: Also including a little admonition for myself,
5.tip: 含めて connects this extra purpose to the main action described afterward.

6.lit: Today, this New Electric Power Company Deluxe Complete Japanese Edition, you know,
6.tip: こちらの introduces the displayed item, and the long phrase following it is the game's title.

7.lit: I think I want to bring you an unboxing review.
7.tip: たいと思います is a common polite way to announce what you intend to do.
